content: Root cause: The bug was caused by the buffer copy functions in the binder driver assuming that the caller would ensure correct alignment and that the memory to be copied was completely within the binder buffer. This assumption was violated by malformed transactions created by users, leading to unexpected behavior and crashes (specifically, triggering a BUG_ON). The patch addresses this by removing the BUG_ON and instead returning an error code, allowing the caller to handle the error appropriately.

Code statements:
```c
-	    !IS_ALIGNED(offset, sizeof(u32)))
-	    binder_alloc_copy_from_buffer(&proc->alloc, object, buffer,
-					  offset, read_size))
-	binder_alloc_copy_from_buffer(&proc->alloc, object, buffer,
-				      offset, read_size);
-	binder_alloc_copy_from_buffer(&proc->alloc, &object_offset,
-				      b, buffer_offset, sizeof(object_offset));
-	binder_alloc_copy_from_buffer(&proc->alloc, &last_obj_offset,
-					      b, buffer_offset,
-					      sizeof(last_obj_offset));
-		binder_alloc_copy_from_buffer(&proc->alloc, &object_offset,
-						   buffer, buffer_offset,
-						   sizeof(object_offset)));
-		binder_alloc_copy_from_buffer(&proc->alloc, &fd, buffer,
-						offset, sizeof(fd));
-		binder_alloc_copy_from_buffer(&target_proc->alloc,
-					      &object_offset,
-					      t->buffer,
-					      buffer_offset,
-					      sizeof(object_offset));
-		binder_alloc_copy_to_buffer(&target_proc->alloc, b, buffer_offset,
-				    &bp->buffer, sizeof(bp->buffer));
-		binder_alloc_copy_to_buffer(&target_proc->alloc,
-						    t->buffer, object_offset,
-						    fp, sizeof(*fp));
-		binder_alloc_copy_to_buffer(&target_proc->alloc,
-						    t->buffer, object_offset,
-						    fp, sizeof(*fp));
-		binder_alloc_copy_to_buffer(&target_proc->alloc,
-						    t->buffer, object_offset,
-						    bp, sizeof(*bp));
-		binder_alloc_copy_to_buffer(&proc->alloc, t->buffer,
-					    fixup->offset, &fd,
-					    sizeof(u32));
```
